quests.title: The Debt of Names

find.text: A scaffold post has been chalked with a tally of a thousand strokes, and beneath it, scratched deep: 'Do not say them aloud. Take the rubbing to the Alessian gate.' A grape leaf is pinned through the tally.

quests.desc: A tally of a thousand names at an abandoned Ayleid dig led me toward an Alessian gate and a family of winemakers.
quests.pitch: Diggers at the cut-away stopped work when someone read a name aloud. They were paid in wine, not coin.

objectives.text: At the Gate of Alma Ruma, match the rubbing to the cut-out page and follow it to a winery.
Drink the Remembrance vintage at Thalaras Winery and follow what it shows.

quests.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The wine, the pool and the Count's silent castle all point at the vault of names under Miscarcand.

quests.title: The Debt of Names (II)
quests.desc: The wine, the pool and the Count's silent castle all point at the vault of names under Miscarcand.
quests.pitch: Diggers at the cut-away stopped work when someone read a name aloud. They were paid in wine, not coin.

objectives.text: Read the names in the mirror pool at night, then carry them to Skingrad.
Slip into the Count's cellar at Skingrad and take the steward's key.
Reach the vault under Miscarcand and settle the Warden's debt.

quests.outro: The last warden fell silent and the plate of names lay in my hands. I could carry it to a priest, a vintner or a flame. What is owed to the dead is a hard thing to settle.

quests.title: The Gate That Was Opened

find.text: A dock lectern holds a salt-stained prayer-sheet to 'the ones the water kept', every line struck through but the last: 'Light the Candle when the tide is out. The door is only latched, not locked.'

quests.desc: A drowned-men's prayer at the Lunar Fang Docks speaks of a door that was only latched. It led me to a hidden sanctuary and a ruined city.
quests.pitch: Fishermen at the Lunar Fang Docks light a single candle each low tide and will not say for whom.

objectives.text: Break the inner coffin-room at the Cyrodiil Sanctuary and read the dead priest's letter.
Climb the Anvil lighthouse and ask who has been lighting it.

quests.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The trail of the Ashen Candle ends at the crater edge where the Gate first opened.

quests.title: The Gate That Was Opened (II)
quests.desc: The trail of the Ashen Candle ends at the crater edge where the Gate first opened.
quests.pitch: Fishermen at the Lunar Fang Docks light a single candle each low tide and will not say for whom.

objectives.text: Wade the Hollow at low tide and carry its bone candle to Kvatch.
Dig through the north ward of Kvatch for the register of the night the Gate opened.
At the crater lip of Kvatch Gate, face the last keeper of the door.

quests.outro: At the crater lip I found the last candle still burning in a ring of lava glass. Whoever latched the door is long dead, but the debt they left is the city's to settle, not theirs.

quests.title: The Dragon-Hunters' Vigil

find.text: A bell without a clapper hangs from the priory orchard wall. Scratched on its rim: 'Seven bells keep the door shut. Four are missing. Ask the statue what it watches.'

quests.desc: A clapperless bell in a priory orchard says seven bells keep a door shut and four are gone. It points to a statue on the Valus road.
quests.pitch: A priory brother says the bell in the orchard rings once a night with no hand on it.

objectives.text: Read the line of the Sentinel's hand and follow it to Bruma.
Find the old Bruma chapel bell and carry its clapper up to the Cloud Ruler.

quests.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The missing bells led from Bruma to a cliff-top keep and a wizard's rock, and on to the old Akaviri fortress.

quests.title: The Dragon-Hunters' Vigil (II)
quests.desc: The missing bells led from Bruma to a cliff-top keep and a wizard's rock, and on to the old Akaviri fortress.
quests.pitch: A priory brother says the bell in the orchard rings once a night with no hand on it.

objectives.text: Ask the Cloud Ruler archivist for the lowest ledger and follow it to the wizard's rock.
Take the Frostcrag bell from the storm-room, or persuade its keeper to part with it.
Hang the seven bells in the deepest nave of Sancre Tor and face what answers.

quests.outro: I set the last bell in its cradle at Sancre Tor and the air, which had been humming for days, went still. Whatever sleeps beneath the barrow, it sleeps for now.

quests.title: The Ring Beneath the Rings

find.text: The innkeeper's accounts hang on a hook: a column headed 'water' where the bridge-inn pays more every season, in a hand that signs only 'by order of the Ring'.

quests.desc: An inn on a bridge pays a water-tax to something called the Ring. The same signature shows up in three cities.
quests.pitch: The innkeeper at the Imperial Bridge Inn says the river is falling, though it rained all week.

objectives.text: Find the clerk's cipher in Chorrol's oak and read the sluice-list.
Lower a bucket in Cheydinhal's refugee well and read the gate-list on the stone.

quests.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The Ring's water runs under every great city and ends beneath the Imperial City itself.

quests.title: The Ring Beneath the Rings (II)
quests.desc: The Ring's water runs under every great city and ends beneath the Imperial City itself.
quests.pitch: The innkeeper at the Imperial Bridge Inn says the river is falling, though it rained all week.

objectives.text: Cut the welded hatch under the Lucky Old Lady and follow the water upriver.
Open the sealed grate under the Waterfront and close the Ring.

quests.outro: Below the Waterfront the old reservoir lay black and still, ringed by sluice-gates stamped with a clerk's seal. I closed one. It was a start, and I left proof for the Palace.
